data.gender_notes: Ursala is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic word ‘ursa’ meaning ‘she-bear’. The name Ursala may symbolize strength and protection, evoking images of a fierce and loving mother bear. The name Ursala carries the meaning “Little she-bear” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ursala usually hope their child will grow to embody little she-bear and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ursala belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little she-bear.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ursala total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: אורסלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: The name Ursala is derived from the Hebrew word 'Urs', meaning bear, and 'la', meaning little. In Hebrew, the name is written as אורסלה (Ursala).

in_greek.name: Οὐρσαλώ
in_greek.long_meaning: The name Ursala in Greek is transliterated as Οὐρσαλώ (Oursalō), which also means 'Little Bear'.

in_latin.name: Ursula
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Ursala in Latin is the same as in English, 'Ursula'. It is derived from the Latin word 'ursus', meaning bear, and 'ula', meaning little. In Latin, the name is written as Ursula.

in_english.name: Ursula
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ursula in English is derived from the Old English word 'urs', meaning bear, and 'wealh', meaning foreigner or stranger. However, it is now commonly understood to mean 'Little Bear'. In English, the name is written as Ursula.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ursala has been popular in European cultures since the Middle Ages, and its popularity was reinforced by the revered figure of St. Ursula, a legendary British princess who, according to Catholic mythology, led a large number of virgin companions on a pilgrimage to Rome to offer herself as a bride to the martyr Saint Tomas of Canterbury. This legendary tale of Ursula's self-sacrifice, bravery, and spiritual devotion has contributed to the enduring appeal of the name.
data.spiritual_significance: The female bear is deeply symbolic in many religious and spiritual traditions around the world. In the Christian context, St. Ursula's name embodies the spiritual strengths of protection, wisdom, and courage. The name Ursala can serve as a reminder to live a life marked by selflessness, devotion, and unwavering faith in the face of challenges. Just as a mother bear defends and nurtures her cubs, the name Ursala inspires us to cherish and protect those we love and to provide strength and guidance when needed.
data.spiritual_symbolism: As a name associated with Saint Saint Ursula and the Eleven Thousand Virgins, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue.
